alt: Black-and-white photo of a box truck crammed under Louisville's Third Street railroad overpass, its roof buckled against the bridge with the LOW CLEARANCE 11-8 ALL TRUCKS sign hanging directly above the point of impact, debris on the road
story: During Louisville's I-65 closure (June–August 2026), GPS rerouted 125,000 daily vehicles past a railroad underpass with 11-foot-8 clearance — peeling the roofs off 45 tractor-trailers in two months while officials' only response was adding more warning signs (now 30+).
why_funny: The official solution to a bridge that destroys roughly one truck per day is to keep stapling more signs to things, earning the bridge its own community memorial website, t-shirt line, and the nickname 'Can Opener' — while the fix (raise or lower the road) sits in the 'too expensive' pile.
